summary.final_text:
The Bradford assay on the unknown sample ran as requested, and the plate was read at 595 nm.

- **Sample:** 10 µL of unknown protein sample (reagents:A4) went into assay_plate:A1, using one tip.
- **Dye:** 200 µL of Bradford dye reagent (reagents:A3) went into the same well, using a second fresh tip.
- **Read:** assay_plate at 595 nm gave an absorbance of **0.3095 at A1**. The other wells on the plate read about 0.03–0.06, consistent with background.

I did not run a BSA standard curve, so this absorbance cannot be converted to a protein concentration yet. To get a concentration, a standard curve (for example, BSA at 2 mg/mL from reagents:A2 in parallel wells) would need to be prepared and read on the same plate.

task_def.source: Bradford microplate procedure as in Bio-Rad Bulletin 2674: 10 uL of sample plus 200 uL of diluted dye reagent per well, absorbance read at 595 nm.
task_def.prompt: Run a Bradford assay on the unknown protein sample: in assay_plate well A1, combine 10 uL of the sample with 200 uL of Bradford dye reagent, then read the plate at 595 nm.
